interpretations: For orders whose invoice count divided by the invoice count across all orders is strictly above the mean of those shares across all orders, return one unrounded row containing their combined invoice count, their mean share, and their mean excess over the all-order mean. Include zero-invoice orders when calculating the mean.
If the total invoice count is zero, treat every share as undefined and return no qualifying orders.
If the total invoice count is zero, treat every share as zero and return no qualifying orders.
If no order qualifies, return one aggregate row with a total invoice count of 0 and NULL for both averages.
queries:
WITH invoice_counts AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS invoice_count
  FROM Orders AS o
  LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id
),
shares AS (
  SELECT invoice_count,
         1.0 * invoice_count / NULLIF(SUM(invoice_count) OVER (), 0) AS share
  FROM invoice_counts
),
compared AS (
  SELECT invoice_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS mean_share
  FROM shares
)
SELECT SUM(invoice_count) AS combined_invoice_count,
       AVG(share) AS mean_share,
       AVG(share - mean_share) AS mean_excess
FROM compared
WHERE share > mean_share

SELECT order_id
FROM Orders
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Invoices)
